nodes.label: Mathematics — Student's Book, Preparatory Year Three (First and Second Term), English medium
Equal ordered pairs
nodes.description: Find unknown values by equating the corresponding components of equal ordered pairs, and plot ordered pairs.

nodes.label: Finding cartesian products
nodes.description: Find the cartesian product X×Y of two finite sets, including X², and calculate the number of its elements n(X×Y).

nodes.label: Arrow and cartesian diagrams
nodes.description: Represent the cartesian product of finite sets by an arrow diagram and a cartesian diagram.

nodes.label: Graphing infinite cartesian products
nodes.description: Represent products of infinite sets such as N×N, Z×Z, Q×Q and R×R on a perpendicular graphical net, identify ordered pairs of points, and locate points by quadrant or axis.

nodes.label: Write relations as ordered pairs
nodes.description: Write a relation from a set X to a set Y as a set of ordered pairs, using the rule connecting a and b (e.g. b = 2a + 4, or 'a is a digit of b').

nodes.label: Represent relations by diagrams
nodes.description: Represent a relation by an arrow diagram and by a cartesian diagram.

nodes.label: Relations as subsets of X × Y
nodes.description: Determine whether a relation is a subset of the cartesian product X × Y, decide which ordered pairs satisfy the stated relation, and identify a relation on a set X as R ⊂ X × X.

nodes.label: Identify functions
nodes.description: Decide whether a relation, given as arrow diagram, cartesian diagram or ordered pairs, is a function by checking that each element of X has only one image.

nodes.label: Symbolic representation of functions
nodes.description: Write a function using the symbols f : X \to Y, f(x) = y and as a set of ordered pairs, and represent it by an arrow diagram and a cartesian diagram.

nodes.label: Domain, codomain and range
nodes.description: Determine the domain, codomain and range of a function, noting the range is a subset of the codomain.

nodes.label: Identify polynomials and degree
nodes.description: Identify polynomial functions and state their degree from the function rule.

nodes.label: Evaluate function values
nodes.description: Calculate the image of a given value (including surds) under a polynomial function.

nodes.label: Graph linear and constant functions
nodes.description: Represent a linear function or constant function graphically by finding ordered pairs and drawing the straight line.

nodes.label: Graph quadratic functions
nodes.description: Represent a quadratic function graphically and state its vertex, axis of symmetry and maximum or minimum value.

B (3, -2) is located in the fourth quadrant.
C (-4, -2) is the located in the third qudrant
D (-4, 3) is the located in the second qudrant
E (0, -3) is the locate on y - axis
F (2, 0) is the located on x - axis.

questions.stem: If $X=[-2, 3]$ find the location which represents $X\times X$. Show which of the following points belongs to the cartesian product of $X\times X$. A (1, 2)
solution: X = [-2, 3] is the real numbers from -2 to 3, so X × X is the square region with x and y both in [-2, 3].
For (1, 2): 1 is in X and 2 is in X.

questions.stem: If $X=[-2, 3]$ find the location which represents $X\times X$. Show which of the following points belongs to the cartesian product of $X\times X$. B (3, -1)
solution: X × X is the square region with x and y both in [-2, 3].
For (3, -1): 3 is in X and -1 is in X.

questions.stem: If $X=[-2, 3]$ find the location which represents $X\times X$. Show which of the following points belongs to the cartesian product of $X\times X$. C (-1, 4)
solution: X × X is the square region with x and y both in [-2, 3].
For (-1, 4): -1 is in X, but 4 is not in X because 4 > 3.
So (-1, 4) does not belong to X × X.

questions.stem: Which of the following functions represents polynomial: $f_1(x)=x^3+x^2+3$
solution: $f_1(x)=x^3+x^2+3$ has powers of x equal to 3, 2 and 0.
These are whole-number powers and the coefficients are real numbers.
So it is a polynomial (of degree 3).
questions.source_note: The book's own exercise (pp3u1-4:drill-1:A, printed p.19); answer generated, both readings agree, not yet reviewed. Compiled from the book record (compile_book_records.py).

questions.stem: Which of the following functions represents polynomial: $F_2(x)=x^3+\frac{1}{x}+7$
solution: The power of x is -1, which is not a whole number.
So it is not a polynomial.

content.text_md: If $X=\{1, 2\}$, $Y\{3, 4, 5\}$ Find: $X\times Y$, and represent it: First: by the arrow diagram. Second: by the cartesian diagram.
Where the cartesian product of X × Y is represented by an arrow diagram, or a grahpical net, as follows:

First: An arrow diagram. Draw an arrow from each element that represents the first projection (The elements of set of X) to each element that represents the second projection (The elements of set of Y)
i.e: The arrow diagram of the cartesian product represents each ordered pair by an arrow that starts from its first projection and ends at the second projection.

Second: Cartesian diagram (the perpendicular graphical net). On a perpendicular graph net, the elements of set X is represented horizontally and the elements of set Y vertically. The intersection points of the horizontal and vertical lines represent the ordered pairs of the elements of the cartesian product X x Y.

content.text_md: How can you represent the cartesian product of each of the following? N × N, Z × Z, Q × Q and R × R.
Draw two perpendicular lines x'x (horizontal) and y'y (vertical) meeting at O, which represents 0.
For N × N, mark the natural numbers on both lines starting from O.
For Z × Z, mark the integers on both lines, with O as (0, 0). The net is the coordinate plane of Z × Z.
For Q × Q, mark the rational numbers on both lines in the same way.
For R × R, mark the real numbers on both lines. The net is divided into four quadrants.
Draw vertical and horizontal lines through the marked points. Each intersection point represents one ordered pair of the product.

content.text_md: Which of the following cartesian diagrams represent a function from X to X.
X = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. A function needs each element of X to appear exactly once as a first coordinate.
Diagram (1): the dots are (3, 5), (4, 4), (2, 3), (1, 2), (3, 2). The element 3 appears twice, with images 5 and 2, and 5 has no dot. So it is not a function.
Diagram (2): the dots are (1, 3), (2, 3), (3, 3), (4, 3), (5, 3). Each of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 appears exactly once. So it is a function.
Diagram (3): the dots are (1, 1), (2, 2), (4, 4), (5, 5). The element 3 has no dot. So it is not a function.
Only diagram (2) represents a function from X to X.
